name: Oxidize
description: Uninstall programs from your PC and clear out what they leave behind, with one button and a backup of everything removed.

hero.lede: Uninstall programs from your PC and clear out what they leave behind. One button removes a program completely, and Undo brings it all back.
notes: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit. One file, nothing to install. The command line is oxidize.exe.
If Windows says it protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway.
hero.away: Oxidize runs on Windows. Open this page on your PC to download it.

features.label: Remove
features.title: One button, one question first
body: Remove completely closes the program's running copies, runs its own uninstaller when it needs one, removes everything found at high confidence and keeps a backup.

main.name: f2
main.alt: The question before Quillmark is removed completely

features.label: Result
features.title: It ends with Nothing left
body: After the removal Oxidize scans again. It says Nothing left, or lists what is still there and why, and counts the lower-confidence items it kept.

main.name: f3
main.alt: The result: Nothing left, eight items removed, with an Undo button

features.label: Leftovers
features.title: Finds what uninstallers leave behind
body: Oxidize looks through the registry, AppData, ProgramData, the Start menu, services, scheduled tasks, firewall rules and PATH.
High-confidence items start ticked; the medium ones wait for you.

main.name: f1
main.alt: Four leftovers of Corvid Notes after its own uninstaller ran, all ticked

features.label: Undo
features.title: Every removal can be undone
body: Before anything is deleted, registry keys are exported and files are moved into a backup folder. Undo puts every item back, and the log names each one.

main.name: f4
main.alt: After Undo, Quillmark is back with everything that belonged to it

features.label: Preview
features.title: See every item before it goes
body: With Dry run on, Remove completely changes nothing. It lists each item it would remove and each running process it would close.

main.name: f5
main.alt: A dry run: eight items would be removed and one running process closed

features.label: Clean up
features.title: Clear out what Windows piles up
body: The Clean up tab measures temporary files, crash dumps, the Recycle Bin, browser caches, Windows' component store, the Delivery Optimization cache, an old Windows installation and folders of removed programs.
The safe ones start ticked. Recent files, a running browser and folders you protect stay, and caches never take cookies, history or logins with them.

main.name: f6
main.alt: The Clean up tab after an analysis: temporary files, crash dumps and browser caches ticked, 1.2 GB in all

assistant.label: AI assistant
assistant.title: Let your assistant clean up
body: oxidize mcp lets an AI assistant on your PC list programs, find leftovers and plan a removal. Nothing goes over the network.
A removal is always a plan first: what goes, with paths, sizes and reasons, and where the backup goes. Your assistant asks you before it carries a plan out, and every removed item is backed up.
The command line has --json on every command. Download the skill to teach your assistant all of it.
assistant.caption: Add Oxidize to your MCP client

pair.label: Themes
pair.title: Follows your Windows theme
body: Oxidize is light or dark, the way Windows is set.

items: A removal never takes the folders Windows keeps for you (Downloads, Saved Games, the cloud folder, the desktops and the rest), wherever they really are, and a folder in Downloads or on a desktop that a removal empties stays.

Clean up walks a temp folder only when it really is one: a profile, a drive or a folder Windows keeps is left alone, with a note saying why. It asks again right before it cleans whether a browser runs.
Restore puts a copy back only from its own backup and only to where it came from, and imports a registry export only into the key it was taken from.
A registry path with an empty part, or a key every program shares, is never deleted.
A file named like the program's but somewhere else, or anything in an install folder whose name says nothing about the program, counts at Medium only.
A working autostart with spaces in its path is no longer taken for a dangling one, and a file on a drive that is not plugged in counts as there.
oxidize mcp refuses --dry-run, --yes and --no-backup, and waits up to 30 minutes for an uninstaller to finish.
The window runs one thing at a time, waits for running work before it closes, and shows an undone cleaning as freeing nothing.

requirements: Administrator rights only for programs installed for all users
No install and no internet connection

privacy.title: Nothing goes online
body: Oxidize has no network code. The assistant connection runs over your PC's own input and output, nothing else.

data.title: Only the backups
body: Each removal gets one backup folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Oxidize\backups, with the exported registry keys, the moved files and a list of every step. Oxidize keeps no other data.

basics.title: Get started
steps: Double-click it. There is nothing to install.
Pick a program and click Remove completely.

basics.title: Updates
body: Download the file again and replace the old one. Every release uses the same file names.

basics.title: Removing it
body: Delete oxidize-gui.exe, and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Oxidize once you no longer need the backups in it.

a: Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT license.

faq.q: Why does Windows say it protected my PC?
a: Oxidize is not signed with a paid certificate, so Windows warns about it the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
Yes. Everything is backed up before it is removed. Click Undo in the window, or use oxidize restore from the command line; oxidize backups lists them.

faq.q: Does it remove things that belong to other programs?
a: Only high-confidence items go by default, each with the reason it matched. Windows' own folders are never touched, and a vendor folder that still holds another product stays.

faq.q: Do I need the command line?
a: No. The window does everything. oxidize.exe is there for scripts, and a zip holds both.
